chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil narrated to me, who said: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'dabadi narrated from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah from Mansur ibn al-Abbas from Sa'id ibn Janah from Husayn ibn Mukhtar from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Three types of people upon whom Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will not look: the one who drags his garment in pride, the one who lowers his skirt in arrogance, and the one who sells his merchandise by swearing oaths. Indeed, pride is for Allah, the Lord of the Worlds.
ai.seo_question: Who are the three types of people Allah will not look at?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights three distinct manifestations of *kibr* (pride)—garment dragging, false commercial oaths, and general arrogance—as barriers to divine gaze, linking physical postures to spiritual states. This narration reinforces the Shia emphasis on *tawhid* in attributes, asserting that while humans may exhibit pride, ultimate majesty and sovereignty belong exclusively to Allah. The inclusion of merchants underscores the social and economic dimensions of pride in early Islamic society, where trade practices were closely monitored for ethical integrity.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 3. It was narrated to me by Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakil who said it was narrated to me by Ali b. al-Hussain al-Sa’dabadi from Ahmad b. Abi Abdillah from Mansur b. al-Abbas from Sa’eed b. Janah from Hussain b. Mukhtar from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said: “

The Almighty Allah will not have mercy on three types of people – the proud, one whose dress of pride sweeps the ground and one who swears in order to sell things. Surely pride is only for the Lord of the Worlds.”
